objective: B197, from MEET-ORDERS-20261118-001 (direction 2), taken after LOCAL-ROOM-20261118-001 by agreement with the coordinator: does a rule that takes only the fills keeping two orders (never nesting one fill inside another, Lemma C), and subdivides when none is left, grow two-way grids without end, as the class law did with memory, or starve? Compared with plain KF3, a subdivide-only baseline, the cheapest steps that keep two orders, and the same rule with no knot-sharing condition. Serves G1 and G16; tests A99.
status: Complete 2026-11-18 (Successful; refereed, R1 confirmed with fixes, no Block): B197 answered yes. The rule that takes only the fills keeping at most two orders, and otherwise lengthens the line by a subdivision, grows full two-way grids and keeps two orders forever: proved with any old pairs (from any line, a full grid before the first lengthening, then every new row or column refilled), computed with knots only on co-knotted pairs (nearly every run to n = 40 from every bracketing of 5 to 8). Nothing per split is handed over or remembered; what is given is the cap of two and the subdivision fallback, and uncapped the same rule makes every order, so the two is the cap's (narrowed after the referee). The corner rule across crossing splits does the same once its first crossing reaches every split. 5 of 8 predictions held.
